brief.ask: Set the art direction for 24 adult party evites: cocktail nights, wine, rooftops, 30/40/50 milestones, casino, disco, tiki, BBQ, masquerade, game night, karaoke, brunch, bonfire, speakeasy, sunset, black tie, retirement, bachelorette, 80s, 90s, whiskey, dinner party.
brief.audience: Adults 25 to 65 inviting friends; the invite is also their taste on display.
brief.feeling: Editorial and grown-up; a magazine spread that moves.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.
references: Exploration grid A: dark plum and gold still lifes, champagne coupes mid-toast, mirrored disco balls, velvet and brass; deep negative space below.
Exploration grid B: overhead candlelit long tables with linen, taper candles, citrus and herbs, hard window-light shadows; food-magazine.

proposals.title: The Governed Plate
proposals.idea: Every one of the 24 evites is derived from a single structural act: one dominant axis — a 35° diagonal cantus firmus — from which the art plate's light source, the foreground drift vector, the foil reveal direction, and the type hierarchy all hang without exception, so that theme changes the content but never dissolves the measure.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 frame divided by a strict 12-column, 6-row modular grid at 390px; the 35° cantus-firmus axis is drawn from lower-left third to upper-right third and governs every diagonal element — bokeh rake, foil shimmer angle, tilt-parallax offset — without negotiation. The lower 30% of every plate is held in deep negative space (≥ 85% luminance shadow) as a dedicated live-text dock: this zone is structurally inviolable across all 24 designs. Visual weight sits in the upper 55%; a transitional 15% band resolves the two registers the way a pediment resolves a colonnade.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL, Google Fonts) — SC caps for event title at 38–44px, tracked +80, set in the negative-space dock. Secondary: DM Sans (OFL) at 13px/20px leading for date, venue, host — weight 300, tracked +20, never baked. The two families share a classical axis ratio: Cormorant carries the ceremony, DM Sans carries the information. No face is decorative; both are load-fast variable fonts. Size relationships follow a strict 1:1.618 modular scale: no intermediate sizes are permitted.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generation in two prompt-grid passes. Grid A (8 plates): extreme close-up still lifes — champagne coupe catching a single point-source at upper-left, cut crystal whiskey glass, disco ball fragment, tiki vessel, casino chip stack — each lit from one motivated source at 35° that matches the cantus-firmus axis. All plates: dark field, specular highlights along the governing diagonal, no lifestyle figures, no faces, no copyrighted objects. Grid B (8 plates): overhead or near-overhead candlelit tablescapes — linen, taper wax drip, citrus cross-section, herb sprigs, card fan, vinyl record edge — hard raking window-light shadows that fall along the 35° axis. Plates are full-bleed art; foreground cut-outs (glass rim, smoke wisp, single leaf, feather mask fragment) are generated separately on transparent fields and composited as Tela drift layers. No lifestyle photography. No faces. Ever
proposals.texture: Simulated: fine-tooth hot-press paper grain at 12% opacity overlay on the art plate (procedural shader, not scanned); micro-halftone dot pattern in the transitional band at 8% opacity to soften the register break without decorating it. WebGL foil shimmer restricted to the specular highlight zone along the 35° axis — it does not migrate. Candle-flicker particle layer (bonfire, speakeasy, dinner party variants) is a procedural shader confined to the upper 40% of frame. No texture is applied uniformly; every material decision is motivated by the plate's light grammar.
proposals.motion: Entrance: art plate fades from black over 400ms (ease-out cubic) — the negative-space dock arrives first, text last, enforcing hierarchy through time. Parallax: foreground cut-out layer drifts on phone tilt along the 35° vector only — no perpendicular drift, no random float; maximum displacement 18px. Foil shimmer responds to tilt at half the displacement rate of the cut-out layer, so the two motions are related by a fixed ratio (1:2) and never compete. Bokeh particles (where present) drift upward at 0.4px/frame, constant, no easing, no burst — sustained breath, not punctuation. All motion honours prefers-reduced-motion: on flag, every layer is static, foil is a fixed gradient, parallax is disabled. Total motion budget: nothing accelerates without a structural reason; nothing lingers past its earned duration.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (8–16 plates each) directed at: (1) extreme close-up specular still lifes on black field, single motivated point-source upper-left, 35° highlight rake, no figures; (2) overhead candlelit tablescapes, hard raking shadow at 35°, food-magazine depth of field. Cut-out foreground elements generated in a third pass on neutral field, background-removed procedurally. WebGL layer: GLSL shader for foil (highlight vector locked to plate's light-source coordinates), bokeh (origin locked to same), particle systems (theme-parametric: bubbles/smoke/embers/confetti). All composited in Tela's layer stack. Live-text zone is a reserved CSS region; no generative text is ever baked into art. Reduced-motion fallback is a CSS class swap, no separate asset needed.
proposals.humanTrace: The governing 35° axis is a director's decision made before any image exists — it is the structural act, the mark of authorship. Within that constraint, the Magnific plates carry physically plausible light: specular bloom, wax-drip translucency, condensation on glass, smoke diffusion — all phenomena that read as having been witnessed even when generated. Editorial selection (which plate, which cut-out, which bokeh depth) is the curator's hand. The type dock spacing is set by eye against the modular scale, not by algorithm alone.
proposals.risk: The single governing axis risks monotony across 24 designs — if the 35° diagonal reads as a template rather than a principle, the collection collapses into wallpaper. The risk is worth carrying because the alternative — 24 independently art-directed evites without a shared structural grammar — produces a product line with no identity, only variety. The cantus firmus is what makes the collection a body of work rather than a folder of assets. The mitigation is in the art plates themselves: theme, subject, colour temperature, and material surface vary enormously within the fixed structure, the way Palladio's villas vary within the same proportional system.

arguesWith.why: The Futurist will want the governing axis to be a dynamic parameter — responsive to content type, user context, or system state — arguing that a fixed 35° is an arbitrary constant masquerading as a principle. proposals.title: Ink Pulled, Not Printed
proposals.idea: Each evite is a simulated hand-pulled proof — the art plate reads as a monotype or screen print caught mid-press, with registration drift, ink drag, and plate tone visible beneath the event's own light source, so the invitation itself is evidence of a decision someone made before the party existed.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 mobile frame. Art plate fills bleed. A single horizon band — roughly the lower 38% of the plate — is treated as the ink-heavy shadow zone (deep negative space, maximum ink deposit). All foreground cut-outs float above this horizon, never below it. Text lives in two locked rows: a tight overline slug at 5% from top, and the event title stacked at 62% — both in the ink-shadow zone so they read against the darkest value. No card, no box, no container. The type sits directly on the plate like a title screen-printed onto the proof itself. Grid exploration uses a 4×4 array of 390×845px crops, each themed plate sharing the horizon-band rule but varying ink color, drag direction, and plate tone.
proposals.typography: Primary: Space Grotesk (OFL, Google Fonts) — condensed weight, tracked +120, all caps for the event title; reads as a stencil cut from the plate. Secondary: Playfair Display (OFL) italic, small, for date/venue overline — the only cursive element, functioning like a handwritten edition note on a print. Scale contrast is brutal: title at ~72px, overline at ~13px. No mid-size. Letterspacing on the title is wide enough that each letter could be a separate block stamp.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates only. Two prompt grids directed as follows — Grid A (12 plates): 'monotype print aesthetic, simulated ink drag and plate tone, [theme object] caught in raking side-light at 35° from left, deep indigo/plum ink ground with [accent color] ink bleed, visible paper tooth through thin ink passages, NO photographic realism, painterly halftone edge, edition-proof feeling, 390×845px portrait' — themes cycle through: cocktail glass, wine decanter, rooftop skyline, birthday cake with candles, poker chips, disco ball, tiki mug, BBQ smoke, masquerade mask, dice and cards, microphone, mimosa tower. Grid B (12 plates): same prompt structure but ink ground shifts to warm black with single-color accent (whiskey amber, bonfire orange, speakeasy green, sunset coral, gold foil simulation) for: whiskey glass, dinner candles, sunset silhouette, black-tie tuxedo lapel, retirement gol
proposals.texture: Simulated monotype plate tone — a mid-value ink film that sits between background and foreground, with visible wipe marks (directional gradient noise, 4–8px frequency, low opacity, baked into the plate at generation). Paper tooth appears in the lightest ink passages as a Perlin-noise grain overlay (film grain shader, ~18% opacity, reduced-motion fallback: static). Ink bleed at object edges: a 2–4px softened halo in the accent color, simulated by the WebGL layer's mask blur. No smooth gradients anywhere — every transition has a material excuse.
proposals.motion: On load: plate fades up in 0.4s, no ease — a hard exposure, like a print coming up in developer. Then ink-drag wipe marks animate once, left to right, 0.6s, opacity 0 to 18% and back to 12% — the press passing over. Foreground cut-outs (the themed object — glass, ball, mask) drift on gyroscope/tilt: ±8px lateral, ±5px vertical, spring physics, 300ms lag behind tilt. WebGL layer: foil shimmer on metallic objects only (disco ball, gold watch, casino chips) — shimmer follows tilt angle, not a loop; it moves when the phone moves. Bokeh particles: 4–7 soft circles in accent color, 18–40px, opacity 0.15–0.4, drift upward at 0.3px/frame. Candle flicker shader on bonfire and dinner plates only: flame alpha oscillates ±6% at 1.8Hz irregular. Reduced motion: all animation off, static plate, foil shimmer locked to 45°.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific prompt grids (Grid A: 12 plates, Grid B: 12 plates) generated in one session — 4×6 layout per grid, 390×845px per cell, flat cost. Editorial cull: select 24 winners, reject any plate where the ink drag reads as decoration rather than process. Each selected plate imported into Tela as the base layer. Foreground cut-outs generated separately as PNG-alpha objects (Magnific, isolated object on transparent ground, same ink aesthetic). WebGL effects (foil, grain, bokeh, flicker) applied via Tela's shader layer with per-template parameter sets. All text is live Tela type, never baked. Tilt parallax wired to Tela's gyro API. QR and link-preview thumbnail auto-crops to the top 390×205px of the plate — the ink-shadow horizon must not appear in that zone, so the thumbnail always reads as the bright, themed object against dark ground.
proposals.humanTrace: The ink drag wipe marks. They are directional, irregular, and baked into the generated plate at prompt level — not a filter applied after. They record the direction a squeegee or brayer was moved across the plate before the image was 'pulled.' A viewer who has ever pulled a monotype will recognize the gesture. The registration drift between the ink ground and the foreground cut-out (a deliberate ±2–4px offset in Tela's layer positioning) reads as the second color not landing exactly — which is what happens on a press.
proposals.risk: Some clients will read 'ink drag' and 'registration drift' as a mistake. The risk is that a birthday host sees imperfection where I see evidence. It is worth it because the alternative — a clean, polished plate with no trace of process — is indistinguishable from a thousand other premium evite templates, and this audience is displaying their taste; if their taste is safe, the invite already told the guests something true. I would rather lose the client who wants polish than win the client who cannot tell the difference.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the ink drag, the wipe marks, and the registration drift and call it noise. They will say the themed object and the type are sufficient. But removal is not the same as decision — a clean plate has no memory of what was done to make it, and these invites need to carry the mark of someone who committed to a direction before the party was planned. proposals.title: Behaviour Before Surface
proposals.idea: Every evite is a physically-simulated instrument: one declared light source and one declared depth-plane stack generate all shimmer angles, all parallax offsets, all bokeh falloff origins, and all motion timing as derivable consequences — the theme changes the content, the system changes nothing.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 viewport divided into three declared depth planes: Plane 0 (background art plate, full-bleed, static), Plane 1 (mid-ground cut-outs, transparent PNGs, tilt gain ×1.4), Plane 2 (foreground floating objects and type container, tilt gain ×2.1). A single golden-ratio vertical axis at x=0.382 anchors all type and hero objects across all 24 cards; the remaining width is negative space that the light source owns. No card breaks this contract.
proposals.typography: Display: Fraunces (OFL, Google Fonts) — variable optical-size axis pushed to 'optical' max for headline weight, tracking −0.03em; the swash terminals catch specular light from the declared source and are shimmer-masked per card. Label/data fields: DM Mono (OFL) at 10px, uppercase, tracking +0.18em — machine-legible, never decorative. Body detail: DM Sans (OFL), 14px, weight 300. No third face. Scale system: 64px / 32px / 14px / 10px — four stops, no interpolation.
proposals.imageLogic: Two Magnific prompt grids, each returning 12 plates. Grid A prompt: 'twelve 9:19.5 portrait plates, extreme deep negative space lower two-thirds, motivated 35-degree upper-left key light, physically accurate specular bloom, subjects: [cocktail coupe, wine decanter, rooftop railing, casino chips, disco ball slice, tiki vessel, smoke curl, masquerade mask fragment, vinyl record cross-section, whiskey pour, bonfire ember field, velvet rope end] — each object isolated on near-black field, no text, no people, photographic product-lighting grammar, ultra-sharp plane of focus at subject centroid, bokeh radius increases with declared z-distance'. Grid B prompt: 'twelve 9:19.5 portrait plates, hard raking window light from upper-left at 35 degrees, overhead editorial food-magazine grammar, subjects: [linen tablecloth with single shadow, taper candle at wax-drip moment, citrus cross-section on sla
proposals.texture: WebGL layer only — no scanned grain, no faux-analog overlay. Three procedural shaders: (1) Anisotropic foil shader: highlight vector derived from declared light azimuth 35°, elevation 22°, gyro-tilt rotates the reflection vector in real time, shimmer confined to a mask drawn over metallic surfaces in the art plate. (2) Volumetric bokeh field: depth-sorted point-light particles, falloff exponent 2.4, origin locked to light-source declaration. (3) Caustic ripple for liquid cards (cocktail, wine, tiki, whiskey): WebGL caustic texture scrolled at 0.6 px/frame, alpha 0.18, clipped to vessel mask. No film grain. No vignette. No fake scratches. If a texture cannot be explained by the declared light source, it is removed.
proposals.motion: Entrance sequence is a single choreographed state-machine, identical contract across all 24 cards, durations tuned per-theme via one multiplier token. State 0→1 (0–320ms): Plane 0 fades from black, easing out-expo. State 1→2 (280–600ms): Plane 1 objects drift up 18px from rest, easing out-quart. State 2→3 (520–900ms): Plane 2 foreground props arrive with 12ms stagger per object, easing out-back tension 1.2. State 3→idle: gyro-tilt loop begins, Plane 1 gain ×1.4, Plane 2 gain ×2.1, foil shader active. Idle micro-motion: bokeh particles drift at 0.3 px/frame upward, caustic scroll on liquid cards. Candle/bonfire cards add a 0.8Hz luminance oscillation on the WebGL layer, amplitude 0.06, affecting only warm-frequency mask. Reduced-motion: all states collapse to single 200ms opacity fade; gyro disabled; shaders render single static frame. No animation references any nostalgic motion conventi
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific grid generations (24 plates + 48 cut-out props) executed with the locked 35-degree light-source prompt contract. Plates imported into Tela as Plane 0 assets. Cut-out PNGs composited as Plane 1 and 2 transparent layers. Three GLSL shaders written once, parameterised by per-card tokens: lightAzimuth, lightElevation, planeCount, bokehDensity, causticActive, flickerHz. Per-theme token file (JSON, 24 entries) drives all visual variation — no per-card shader rewrite. Live text layer in Tela pulls host-entered name/date/venue strings; Fraunces variable font renders at runtime. Link preview: Tela generates a static rasterised frame at State 2 (mid-entrance) for OG image. QR lands on the live URL.
proposals.humanTrace: The 35-degree upper-left light-source declaration is a human editorial act, made once, that propagates deterministically through every downstream parameter. The selection of which Magnific plate survives the grid — which coupe angle, which wax-drip moment, which ember field — is curatorial judgment under a strict physical constraint. The shimmer mask drawn over metallic surfaces is hand-authored per plate, not auto-detected. The per-theme token values (flickerHz: 0.8 for bonfire, causticActive: true for tiki, bokehDensity: 0.4 for black-tie) are editorial decisions encoded as data. The human trace is the physics contract and the selection eye, not the hand.
proposals.risk: The system is unforgiving: if any card violates the light-source contract — a shimmer angle that doesn't match the declared azimuth, a shadow falling the wrong way on a cut-out prop — the coherence breaks and the whole series reads as inconsistent rather than systematic. The risk is worth it because the alternative — 24 independently art-directed cards — produces 24 different personalities and no series identity. A single physical contract makes the collection legible as a platform, not a portfolio of one-offs. The secondary risk is that 'no nostalgia' reads as cold to the 25-65 audience. I accept this because the foil shimmer, the bokeh warmth, and the Fraunces swash carry enough sensory richness that the system feels luxurious rather than clinical.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a reveal moment per card — a curtain pull, a masked transition, a crescendo that is specific to each theme's emotional register. I expect the argument that my state-machine entrance is the same choreography for disco and dinner party and that this sameness kills the drama. My counter: the drama is in the content of each plate and the physics of each shimmer, not in

proposals.title: Field Notes From the Table
proposals.idea: Each evite is a documentary plate — a specific, located, materially honest image of a real-world festive tradition, treated with the discipline of a photobook spread, not a party-supply aesthetic.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 phone canvas divided by a hard horizon line at the golden ratio (roughly 61% from top): the upper field holds the art plate full-bleed; the lower negative space — deep and uncluttered — holds all live text. No bleed-through, no layering of type over image. The horizon line itself is a hairline rule, 0.5px, that shifts 4px on tilt. Foreground cut-outs (a coupe rim, a candle flame, a tiki vessel lip, a dice edge) break the horizon upward only, never downward, preserving the reading zone. The 24 designs share this grid as a constant — the variable is what occupies the upper field and which cut-out crosses the line.
proposals.typography: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) for the event title: tracked wide at 9% in small caps, 28–32px, set in the lower field against near-black. IBM Plex Mono (OFL) for date, time, venue: 11px, regular weight, one line each, 14px leading — the mono face reads as a field-notebook coordinate, not a label. No decorative script anywhere. The type is never baked; it lives in Tela's live layer. For the 80s and 90s designs only, Boogaloo (OFL) replaces Cormorant for the title only, tracked tight at −2%, as a period-specific nod that is still legible and does not cosplay.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates directed as documentary still lifes — not fantasy, not CGI chrome, not stock-party-photo. Each plate is directed with a specific location logic: the Tiki plate references mid-century Polynesian-American bar culture of the 1950s Los Angeles tiki revival (Trader Vic's aesthetic, not Hawaiian sacred imagery — that line is hard and I will hold it if the Baroque Dramatist reaches for a lei or a tiki god carving without a collaboration conversation). The Masquerade plate references Venetian cartapesta mask-making, Carnivale di Venezia, not generic feather masks. The BBQ plate is a low overhead of a cast-iron grate with char marks and smoke curl, not red-white-checked tablecloth nostalgia. The Speakeasy plate is a 1920s American bar still life: a cut-crystal lowball, a matchbook, a brass tap handle — no appropriated jazz-club imagery. Magnific prompt discipline: every
proposals.texture: Simulated: a light grain field (film-stock noise, ~18% opacity) is applied as a WebGL shader over the entire canvas — it reads as analog without claiming to be a scan. The lower text field has a faint paper tooth texture (procedurally generated micro-roughness, not a scanned paper — generative only) at 8% opacity so the mono type sits on something, not on pure digital black. Foil shimmer is masked strictly to reflective objects in the plate (coupe rim, mirror ball fragment, casino chip edge, whiskey glass meniscus) — never applied as a decorative field. The foil WebGL mask is generated from the luminance map of the art plate, so it inherits the plate's physical logic rather than floating independently.
proposals.motion: Entrance: the art plate fades in over 600ms with a very slight upward drift of 6px — unhurried, editorial, like turning a page. The horizon hairline draws left to right over 400ms after the plate settles. Tilt/gyro: foreground cut-outs shift 0–8px on a 60ms ease, the art plate shifts 0–3px in the opposite direction — a shallow parallax that suggests depth without spectacle. WebGL foil shimmer is continuous but subtle: a slow sine-wave highlight sweep every 4 seconds, 0.3s duration, tied to the motivated light angle. Candle flicker (bonfire, dinner party, speakeasy designs): a procedural noise shader modulates the warm light leak at 0.8–1.2Hz — irregular, not looping, so it reads as flame not animation. Reduced motion: all parallax and shimmer off; the plate is static; only the horizon line draw plays, once, on load. No motion is decorative; every motion has a physical referent.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific draft grids of 12 plates each, directed with explicit light-source angle, material specificity, and location reference in every prompt. Plates upscaled to 1200×2133px. WebGL layer written as a single reusable shader with parameters (foil mask luminance threshold, light angle in degrees, grain intensity, flicker frequency) that are set per-design in a JSON config — so all 24 designs share one shader build and one cost. Foreground cut-outs are Magnific-generated on transparent backgrounds (subject isolation pass), not hand-cut. Tela document structure: layer 1 art plate, layer 2 cut-outs with tilt binding, layer 3 WebGL shader canvas, layer 4 live text. The 30/40/50 milestone family is a single Tela template with a numeral token that the host sets — the art plate and WebGL config are identical across the three.
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source angle — chosen editorially, named in the Magnific prompt, locked into the WebGL shader config, visible in the parallax shadow direction — is the human trace. It is a physical decision that propagates honestly through every production layer. The grain field and paper tooth are not scanned artifacts but are calibrated to a specific analog referent (Kodak Portra 400 grain structure for the warm-palette designs; Ilford HP5 for the cooler ones) named in the shader parameters. The editorial selection of which 12 plates from the Magnific grid advance is itself a perceptible act of judgment: the rejects will be documented in a Plajah design log so the decision is attributable.
proposals.risk: The restraint will read as cold to hosts who want maximalism — especially for the Bachelorette and Disco designs, where the market expectation is glitter-forward. The risk is worth it because the brief says the invite is the host's taste on display, and taste is demonstrated by what is withheld as much as what is shown. The Baroque Dramatist will push hard for more drama on exactly those two designs and I will listen, but I will not let the foil mask escape the motivated light logic just to add sparkle.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will reach for the Tiki plate and want to add a carved tiki god figure for drama — and I will stop that cold. Tiki god imagery belongs to specific Polynesian carving traditions and a living community; it cannot appear in a generative plate without a collaboration conversation that has not happened. proposals.title: The Curtain Rises, Every Time
proposals.idea: Each invite is a miniature opera house: a single dramatically lit art plate — deep negative space, one motivated light source, physically-plausible material — revealed by a vertical curtain-pull gesture, so the guest becomes the stagehand who opens the show.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:16 stage, full-bleed. A heavy vertical axis bisects the composition — not centered but at a golden 38% — so every plate reads as a wing and a stage simultaneously. The art plate occupies the upper 72% with a hard horizon line (1px foil-shimmer rule at 35°) separating it from a deep negative-space footer that functions as the proscenium lip: all live text — name, date, venue — sits below that rule, spoken from the stage edge. Foreground cut-out objects (a coupe glass, a mask, a disco ball, a tiki idol, a poker chip stack) float 18–24px above the plate plane and drift ±6px on tilt, creating measurable depth without breaking the frame. No card-within-card, no nested rectangles: one stage, one depth axis, one curtain.
proposals.typography: Primary display: Cormorant Garamond (OFL) — italic, tracked loose at +60, set large enough that a single word bleeds off one edge of the 390px frame, creating scale through cropping rather than size alone. Supporting hierarchy: DM Mono (OFL), caps, tight tracking, 11px, used only for date/time/venue as a deliberate counterpoint — the playbill's printed logistics against the hand-lettered marquee. No third face. The display line is never centred: it anchors to the 38% vertical axis and runs diagonally 2° off horizontal, a stage-painted lean that implies the rake of a real floor.
proposals.imageLogic: Generative art plates directed as physically-plausible still lifes under a single off-camera motivated light source — always upper-left at approximately 40° elevation — so shadow direction, foil shimmer angle, bokeh origin, and WebGL light-leak vector are all consistent children of one fictional lamp. The 24 plates are commissioned in two Magnific draft grids of 12: Grid A (dark, nocturnal: plum velvet, whiskey glass, masquerade mask, casino felt, disco ball, black-tie gloves, rooftop skyline silhouette, speakeasy brass, karaoke microphone, bachelorette champagne tower, 80s neon arcade, 90s cassette) and Grid B (warm, textural: tiki cup on rattan, BBQ smoke and ember, bonfire spark trail, sunset citrus, brunch linen and poached egg, wine decanter with sediment, long dinner-party table from above, retirement gold watch close-up, birthday candle on a cut cake, milestone numerals in aged br
proposals.texture: Two texture registers, never mixed within a single plate: Nocturnal plates carry simulated velvet nap (procedural shader: anisotropic micro-fibre, direction follows the 38% vertical axis), lacquered brass reflection, and deep film grain (ISO 3200 simulation, luminance channel only). Warm plates carry linen weave (procedural: irregular warp/weft, slight cream cast), candle-wax drip topology, and salt-halation bloom at highlight edges. The WebGL foil shimmer is a shared production asset — a 35° angle shimmer that propagates across the 1px horizon rule and any metallic object in the foreground cut-out layer — so the material register changes per plate but the light grammar stays constant. This is the human trace made systemic: one fictional lamp, everywhere.
proposals.motion: The reveal is a curtain-pull: on load, two vertical panels — simulated heavy velvet, procedurally rendered with gravity-correct drape — part from the 38% axis outward at 600ms ease-out-expo, exposing the art plate beneath. This is not a fade, not a zoom: it is a theatrical open. Once revealed: foreground cut-outs drift on gyroscope tilt at ±6px, 200ms spring, no easing overshoot; the WebGL foil shimmer breathes at 4-second sine cycle, amplitude tied to ambient light sensor where available; candle-flicker or ember-spark particles (12–16 per frame, physics-sim, 0.4px max radius) rise from any heat-source object in the plate. The display typography fades up 300ms after curtain completes — the marquee lights after the curtain, not before. On reduced-motion: curtain panels are static at 50% open, foreground cut-outs are fixed, shimmer is replaced by a single static foil gradient, no particles
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific generative grid runs (12 plates each, single flat cost): prompts are written with explicit light-source position, material, depth-of-field, and composition instructions to guarantee systemic coherence across all 24. Foreground cut-outs are extracted from the same generated plates using generative segmentation — no separate shoot, no stock library. Velvet curtain panels are procedural shader renders (GLSL, Plajah-owned), using physically-based cloth simulation baked to a 600ms sprite sheet. The 1px foil rule and WebGL shimmer layer are shared Tela components, parameterized by shimmer angle and colour temperature per plate. Cormorant Garamond and DM Mono are loaded from Google Fonts CDN, subsetted to Latin + numerals. Live text fields (name, date, venue) are Tela native — never baked. Total generative asset cost: two Magnific grid runs plus shader compile time.
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source is a directorial decision — chosen, named, held constant across 24 plates — and its angle (upper-left, 40°) is visible in every shadow, every foil shimmer vector, every bokeh origin. This is not algorithmic consistency; it is the equivalent of a cinematographer placing a practical lamp and refusing to move it. The curtain-pull timing (600ms ease-out-expo) was arrived at by counting real curtain pulls on stage footage and matching the weight of velvet. The 2° typographic lean was set by eye against the rake of a real theatre floor. These are decisions, not parameters, and a maker encountering the work will feel them as decisions.
proposals.risk: The curtain-pull reveal risks feeling theatrical in the wrong register — stage-costume rather than editorial — if the art plates beneath are not genuinely stunning enough to justify the ceremony of opening them. The answer is in the prompt discipline: if the plates are flat, the curtain condemns them. This risk is worth carrying because the alternative — a beautiful plate that simply fades in — makes the guest a viewer, not a participant. The curtain makes them the stagehand. That is the difference between receiving an invitation and opening one.

I reject this specifically: the Minimalist is right that a weak gesture is worse than no gesture, but wrong to conclude that no gesture is therefore safer. proposals.title: One Rule, Held Still
proposals.idea: Every card is governed by a single declared geometric constraint — one angle, one axis, one ratio — that propagates without exception into the plate composition, the foreground cut-out position, the WebGL light origin, and the live text alignment, so that the invitation's visual authority comes not from decoration but from the traceable discipline of a single held line.
proposals.geometry: Each card begins with one structural line: a specific angle (15°, 35°, 52°, 72°, or 90°) chosen per theme and declared before any element is placed. That line defines the horizon of the image plate, the drift axis of foreground cut-outs, the rake of the WebGL light source, and the baseline or optical margin of the live type. The 390px column is divided into two unequal horizontal registers — 62% image field, 38% silence — the silence never filled. No decorative borders. The only grid is the one line.
proposals.typography: Space Grotesk (Google Fonts / OFL) for event name: 28–34px, tracked +80, uppercase, set flush to the structural axis not to the screen edge. Cormorant Garamond (Google Fonts / OFL) Italic for host phrasing and subtext: 16–18px, optically placed at the negative-space threshold. No weight above SemiBold. No centred type except on the 90° (perfectly vertical) card — the Black Tie — where centering is the one permitted exception because the geometry earns it.
proposals.imageLogic: Magnific generative plates directed as constrained still-life compositions: the structural angle is baked into the composition brief for each plate — a coupe glass at 35°, a taper candle shadow at 52°, a disco ball reflection arc at 15°. Two Magnific draft grids of 12 plates each: Grid A covers the atmospheric interiors (cocktail, speakeasy, masquerade, black tie, whiskey, dinner party, wine, casino, rooftop, sunset, brunch, bachelorette); Grid B covers the textural outdoors and vernacular (BBQ, bonfire, tiki, 80s, 90s, game night, karaoke, retirement, and the three milestones). Every plate is cropped to leave the lower 38% as structural silence — near-black, near-white, or a single deep field tone — where live text lives. No full-bleed chaos. The plate is the argument; the silence is the counter-argument.
proposals.texture: Simulated: a single 2px grain layer at 14% opacity applied uniformly across all plates via WebGL shader — not decorative grain, grain as a unifying skin that makes generated plates feel like one printed series. Foil shimmer is a hairline refraction, not a flood: it traces only the declared structural line, appearing on the glass rim, the candle edge, or the architectural seam that already follows that angle. Velvet and brass surface suggestions exist only where the plate brief calls for them; they are never added to cards that earned their mood from absence.
proposals.motion: Gyroscope-driven parallax on foreground cut-outs moves only along the declared structural axis — a coupe drifts at 35°, not freely. The WebGL light source shifts with tilt but its origin point is locked to the declared angle. Nothing rotates freely. Entrance: image plate fades from black in 400ms, foreground cut-outs resolve 200ms later, type renders last at 600ms — always last, always earned. Reduced motion: all parallax and shimmer halt; plate and type remain; the card is still legible and still considered. Candle flicker (bonfire, dinner party, speakeasy) is a 3–5% luminance oscillation on a masked region, 0.8–1.4s irregular interval — perceptible but not distracting.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompt grids, 12 plates each, directed with explicit angle, subject, field tone, and silence-zone specifications per theme. WebGL layer: GLSL fragment shader for grain unification, foil hairline traced procedurally along the declared angle vector, bokeh particles positioned at the light-source origin. Foreground cut-outs are Magnific-isolated subject elements (glass, flower, mask, hat, dice) placed as transparent PNG layers in Tela, drift physics constrained to the structural axis. Live text in Tela, never baked. All assets generative or Plajah-owned 3D renders.
proposals.humanTrace: The structural line for each card is hand-declared by the art director before any generation begins — it is a decision, not an output. That declaration is the editorial act. The grain shader is calibrated per session by eye until it reads as print rather than filter. The silence zone is protected by a Tela layer lock that cannot be overridden by content entry — the host cannot accidentally fill the silence. The trace is the held discipline, not a visible gesture.
proposals.risk: The risk is that restraint reads as coldness for party themes that culturally demand warmth — tiki, BBQ, 80s, karaoke. Worth it because the structural line, when held, gives warmth somewhere to stand; without it, warmth becomes noise. The further risk is that hosts who want visual abundance will feel the card is 'empty.' That is the correct tension. The silence is the taste-signal; it is the reason the invite functions as a display of the host's judgment, not just their enthusiasm.

A card that requires two competing light sources to feel dramatic has not found its one contrast — it has avoided finding it. disputes.objection: The curtain-pull is the reveal announcing itself — the structural problem I have always named. When the gesture of opening becomes the dominant experience, the composition beneath it is subordinated to its own entrance, and what should be the primary fact — the image, the hierarchy, the light grammar — arrives as aftermath rather than argument. A 600ms theatrical mechanism is not pacing; it is imposition, and it trains the viewer to expect ceremony before content every single time, which means the second viewing is already diminished. disputes.concession: The insistence on one motivated light source at a fixed angle, held without negotiation across all 24 plates so that shadow direction, shimmer vector, and bokeh origin are all children of one fictional lamp, is exactly the kind of governing constraint I demand — it is the cantus firmus of the system

disputes.objection: The shimmer mask is 'hand-authored per plate' but the foil never touches anything that was risked — no torn edge, no uneven ink deposit, no surface that resisted the tool; it is a clean luminance calculation wearing the word 'hand' as a costume, and a system that removes film grain because it cannot be explained by the declared light source has confused physical plausibility with physical evidence — scars don't need a reason, they just happened. When the only human trace is a physics contract and a selection eye, the work has no body, only behaviour, and behaviour without a body is not making, it is modelling.

disputes.objection: The curtain-pull is a reveal with no rule behind it — it is pure spectacle dressed as interaction. The 600ms ease-out-expo was 'arrived at by counting real curtain pulls,' which means the timing was calibrated to imitate a physical object rather than derived from a system property of the design itself; that is nostalgia for theatre mechanics, not a generative constraint. When I ask what the curtain does when the input changes — when the theme shifts from speakeasy to BBQ — the answer is nothing, it stays a curtain, which means the interaction is a costume over the content, not a behaviour produced by it.
disputes.concession: The discipline of one motivated light source at a fixed angle, held as a generative contract across all 24 plates so that shadow direction, foil shimmer vector, and bokeh origin are all derivable consequences of that single declaration, is exactly right — that is a system, and I will defend it again

synthesis.direction: One declared light source — upper-left, 35° azimuth, 22° elevation — propagates as the physical law of the entire collection: every shadow angle, foil shimmer vector, bokeh falloff origin, and tilt-parallax gain ratio across all 24 evites is a derivable consequence of that single declaration. Three depth planes (background plate, mid-ground cut-outs at tilt ×1.4, foreground props at tilt ×2.1) create measurable spatial depth without theatrical ceremony. Two Magnific grid runs of 12 plates each — extreme specular still lifes and overhead editorial tablescapes — are directed with the light-source contract locked in every prompt; the 24 surviving plates are selected by curatorial eye, not algorithm. Type stack: Fraunces variable (display, 64px, swash terminals shimmer-masked per card), DM Mono (data fields, 10px, uppercase), DM Sans (body detail, 14px weight 300); live in Tela, never baked; lower 38% of every card is a structurally locked text dock.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The Rebel's insistence that the registration drift between art plate and foreground cut-out reads as a committed physical fact — a deliberate ±2–4px offset in Tela layer positioning that implies the second colour not landing exactly — survives as a production parameter. It gives the system a body, not just behaviour.
synthesis.editorCut: The Radical Minimalist removed the entrance state-machine's per-theme timing-multiplier token and collapsed it to a single 400ms fade-in for all 24 cards. The argument: if the choreography varies per theme, the system is no longer a system — it is 24 individual performances wearing a shared costume. The multiplier felt like flexibility; it was actually inconsistency. One entrance contract, identical across all cards, is what makes the collection legible as a platform.

synthesis.ariaSummary:
The team landed on the Futurist's proposal as lead — a single declared light source that acts as physical law across all 24 evites, so every shimmer angle, every shadow, every parallax gain ratio is a consequence of one editorial decision made before any image exists. That constraint is what makes this a collection rather than a folder. I took that side because the brief asks for a product line with identity, and identity requires a rule that does not negotiate with content.

The sharpest disagreement was between the Futurist and the Rebel. The Rebel argued that a system with no film grain, no ink drag, no surface that resisted the tool has no body — only behaviour — and that behaviour without a body is not making, it is modelling. The Futurist held that the physics contract and the curatorial eye are the human trace. I split it: the Futurist's light-source system stands, but the Rebel's registration drift — that deliberate ±2–4px offset between plate and cut-out layer — stays in as a production parameter. It is the one place the system shows a scar.

The Radical Minimalist edited one thing that mattered: the per-theme entrance timing multiplier is gone. One entrance contract across all 24 cards. The Minimalist's argument was clean — a multiplier that varies per theme is not a system, it is 24 individual performances. I agreed. The drama lives in the plates and the physics, not in the choreography.

Two Magnific grid runs (12 plates each) are directed with the light-source contract locked in every prompt. Three GLSL shaders — anisotropic foil, volumetric bokeh, caustic ripple for liquid cards — are written once and parameterised by a per-theme JSON token file. All text is live in Tela. The one thing left for you to decide is the display face.

quotes.line: The 35-degree upper-left light-source declaration is a human editorial act, made once, that propagates deterministically through every downstream parameter.
When the only human trace is a physics contract and a selection eye, the work has no body, only behaviour, and behaviour without a body is not making, it is modelling.
